heard: There is a planet where the atmosphere is made of iron gas. 640 light years away in Pisces, gas giant WASP-B orbits its star in 1.8 days. Blasted by radiation, this world has inflated to nearly twice the diameter of Jupiter. One side is trapped in eternal daylight, soaring past 2,400 degrees Celsius. This inferno is hot enough to rip molecules apart and vaporize solid iron. Ferocious winds sweep that metallic gas to the night side, where it cools to 1,500 degrees. Researchers using the very large telescope detected iron at dusk, but nothing at dawn. They concluded that as the gas cools, it condenses into torrential rains of liquid iron. These metallic winds confirmed a cycle that never ends on this world.
